players.note: In his last two games, Cam Skattebo has been the RB6 and RB10 in weekly scoring while averaging 19.5 touches and 121.5 total yards. In those games, he has had a 72.1% snap rate, 57.4% of the rushing work, and a 46.5% route share (7.8% target share). I expect him to have a similar workload this week. Among 51 qualifying rushers, Skattebo is 18th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Against an elite run defense this week that will unveil Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates, Skattebo is a volume-based RB2. Across their last five games, the Jags have allowed the seventh-lowest rushing success rate while logging the fourth-highest hit rate at or behind the line of scrimmage and ranking 16th in yards after contact per attempt.

Jonathan Taylor is the RB11 in fantasy points per game, despite the Colts' broken team and offense. Last week, he played 66.7% of the snaps with 47.1% of the rushing work and a 76% route share (18.2% target share). Taylor is still splitting early down work with Seth McGowan despite the Colts refusing to trade him. He has a strong 13.9% explosive run rate and 18% missed tackle rate. Despite Daniel Jones, Taylor should still produce RB1/2 numbers this week. Houston's run defense has been more pliable recently. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the 12th-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate.

Garrett Wilson is the WR20 in fantasy points per game, sporting a 27.5% target share with 2.18 YPRR, eight red zone targets, 13 deep targets, and a 34.7% first-read share. There was some debate in the middle of the season, but Wilson is their undisputed WR1. The on-paper matchup is glorious. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. With Geno Smith back, Wilson is a top-15 wide receiver this week with WR1 upside.

Last week, the Jets' backfield tilted back further in favor of Breece Hall. Hall finished with a 58.8% snap rate, 47.8% of the rushing work, and a 43.8% route share. Those numbers all eclipsed Braelon Allen's usage. Hall finished with 15 touches and 108 total yards. Hall has only managed a woeful 1.66 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate this season. He's a volume play at running back again this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have fielded a middle-of-the-road run defense, allowing the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt while ranking 16th in rushing yards over expectation per attempt, 15th in rushing success rate, and 18th in missed tackle rate.

Tetairoa McMillan's production has been crushed, with Bryce Young struggling behind a woeful offensive line. Since Week 7, McMillan has been the WR39 in fantasy points per game. In these four games, he has had a 20.6% target share with 1.40 YPRR, two red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 28% first-read share. This could be a bounce-back game for Young, which should fuel McMillan's stat line. Across their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 4, Ollie Gordon has been the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19.1 touches and 89.8 total yards. Last week, with Kyle McCord under center, Gordon saw a nice bump in his passing game usage with a 12.1% target share, a 21% TPRR, and 39 receiving yards. It was his highest receiving yardage output of the season and his second-highest target share and TPRR of the season. If Gordon is going to see some checkdowns weekly, it'll be a huge add to his weekly floor and ceiling. Prior to last week's game, he hadn't had more than 14 receiving yards in any game this season. Among 51 qualifying backs, Gordon is 12th in explosive run rate and 30th in missed tackle rate. Gordon should have another solid week. Over their last five games, Buffalo has ranked 18th in yards after contact per attempt while allowing the sixth-highest rushing success rate and missed tackle rate.

Last week, with Josh Downs playing, Rashee Rice had a 17.1% target share, 82 receiving yards (3.57 YPRR), a 19% first-read share, and he ran 69.6% of his routes from the perimeter. I expect his usage as an outside receiver to continue as Downs takes the slot role. Rice still had a 33.3% designed target rate, but he also had a 9.17 aDOT, so it wasn't just low aDOT gadget stuff. Rice was the WR23 in weekly scoring. Rice could easily be a WR2 again this week. In their last five games, Arizona has allowed the seventh-most yards per target and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since his Week 8 return, DJ Moore has been the WR19 in fantasy points per game with a 20.9% target share, 2.74 YPRR, three red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 25% first-read share. He has surpassed 80 receiving yards and scored a touchdown in two of those three games. Moore should crush again this week. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 13th-most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.
The Titans are hopeful that Carnell Tate will return this week (shoulder). He opened this week with a limited practice. I'll update his outlook on Friday.

David Montgomery will be back this week. With Woody Marks out, I expect Montgomery to lead the backfield in touches this week, but we'll likely see Emari Demercado mixed in. Montgomery hasn't been effective when on the field this season. He has only a 2.1% explosive run rate, 1.65 yards after contact per attempt, and a 13% missed tackle rate. The context that needs to be applied here, though, is that the offensive line has given him zero room to operate with only 1.00 yards before contact per attempt on his carries, and he has been hit at the line or behind it with 53.8% of his carries. Montgomery should have some room to get loose this week, though. The Colts' run defense has fallen apart. Over their last two games, they have allowed the ninth-most rushing yards, the ninth-highest explosive run rate, and the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt. Montgomery should see 12-15 touches in this game and return decent RB2 production.

Stefon Diggs is the WR24 in fantasy points per game. Since Week 7, he has led the team with a 21.6% target share with 2.12 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 23.6% first-read share. Diggs has run 61.3% of his routes from the slot in his last three games. He won't be shadowed by DJ Turner, who has only seen 3.3% of his snaps in the slot this season. Diggs should eat this week. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the 11th-most yards per target and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Last week, Omarion Hampton had EASILY his best game of the 2026 season as the RB13 for the week. Hampton had 23 touches (22 carries), 105 total yards, and a score. That's the positive news. Ok, now it's time for the bad. Hampton played 63% of the snaps in a game that they played with a lead in. He had 64.7% of the rushing work, BUT he had only a 33% route share, which equaled the route share for Keaton Mitchell and was behind Kimani Vidal (40.7%). This all quietly says that Hampton is game script sensitive and could still be crushed in any game moving forward in which the Bolts are trailing. It's sad, but true. The good thing for Hampton is hopefully the Bolts are playing with a lead this week, and it's a nice matchup for him on the ground. Hampton has 2.22 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate this season (OOF!). The Jets still have a woeful run defense, so hopefully Hampton can take advantage. Over their last five games, the Jets have allowed the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the fourth-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards before contact per attempt.

Last week, Jordyn Tyson's snap rate and usage exploded. Tyson was the WR12 last week while seeing a 72.1% snap share and route share. He gobbled up a 37.1% target share with 80 receiving yards (2.58 YPRR), one red zone target, two deep targets, and a 41.7% first-read share. Tyson also had a 23.1% designed target rate as Kellen Moore was looking to get the ball in his hands early and often. Tyson should eat again this week. Over their last five games, Chicago has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

I expect Saquon Barkley to be back to his workhorse status this week. He opened this week with a full practice. In his last game played, he had a 57.6% snap rate, 52% of the rushing work, and a 31.3% route share (2.9% target share). Barkley finished with a disappointing 13 touches and 22 total yards. This season, he has logged a disappointing 2.04 yards after contact per attempt with a respectable 17% missed tackle rate. Barkley is a volume-driven RB2 option this week with a tough matchup. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the fourth-lowest rushing success rate, the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, and the 11th-fewest yards after contact per attempt and missed tackle rate.

Since his soft benching in Week 8, Ashton Jeanty has reclaimed his lead back role for the Raiders. Their horrible offensive line hasn't allowed for any more running room or production, though. In his last two games, Jeanty has played 68.9% of the snaps with a 60.6% route share (18% target share). He has averaged 12 touches and 42 total yards (zero touchdowns). Jeanty has only a 4.5% explosive run rate, 2.11 yards after contact per attempt, and an 11% missed tackle rate. Jeanty is just a volume-driven flex with a horrible matchup. Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the tenth-lowest rushing success rate, the 14th-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the fourth-fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Jameson Williams is the WR25 in fantasy points per game, overall. Since Week 4, Williams is the WR18 in fantasy points per game with an 18.3% target share, 2.18 YPRR, nine red zone targets, ten deep targets, and a 23% first-read share. Tampa Bay has the second-highest single high rate in the NFL (63.4%). Since Week 4, against single-high, Williams has been second on the team with a 20% TPRR and 2.01 YPRR. Another feather in his cap this week during that stretch is that his TPRR has risen from 17% to 24% when Jared Goff has been blitzed while posting 1.86 YPRR. Williams can have a solid game this week, but I'm not expecting a monster outing. Over their last five games, Tampa Bay has held perimeter wide receivers to the 12th-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

In Jalon Daniels' three starts, Emeka Egbuka was the WR81, WR15, and WR12 in weekly scoring. In one of those games, he was saved by a 14-yard rushing score. Egbuka did have a 30.5% target share with 0.95 YPRR, four red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 39.1% first-read share. The volume is nice to see, and he'll need all of it this week. In their last five games, Detroit has allowed the second-fewest yards per target and the fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Egbuka is a volume-based flex this week with a tough matchup. *UPDATE: Let's also discuss Egbuka's production and such with Baker Mayfield under center in case he does play this week. In the four games Egbuka has played with Mayfield this season, he has had a 19.1% target share, 1.47 YPRR, three red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 22.2% first-read share. Jalon Daniels has leaned on Egbuka more in his starts. With Mayfield's injury-depleted state, I don't think there's a massive divide in quarterback play for Egbuka. If Mayfield draws the start, Egbuka is still somewhere in the WR3 area code.

Since Caleb Williams' return, Rome Odunze has been the WR36 in fantasy points per game. In those four games, Odunze has had a 15% target share, 1.99 YPRR, three red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 15.5% first-read share. Odunze should have a wonderful Week 11. Across their last five games, the Saints have allowed the third-most deep passing yards and the seventh-highest deep passing success rate, so Odunze's downfield role will come in handy this week. During the same span, the Saints have allowed the 14th-most yards per target to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Caleb Douglas's return, he has been the clear WR1 for the team with a 20.5% target share, 2.54 YPRR, one red zone target, seven deep targets, and a 28.8% first-read share. Last week, in Kyle McCord's first start, Douglas had a 21.2% target share, 71 receiving yards (2.45 YPRR), five deep targets, and a 35% first-read share. Douglas should see plenty of volume this week as Miami plays catch-up. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the 13th-most receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers while holding the position to the eighth-fewest yards per target. Douglas is a volume-driven flex play this week. Douglas does get a small bump this week as Christian Benford will be out (groin).

Jaylen Waddle will be back this week (concussion). He practiced in full all week. In Weeks 1-8, he was the WR42 in fantasy points per game with an 18.8% target share, a 24% TPRR, 1.62 YPRR, four red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 28.6% first-read share. During that stretch, he had only four weeks as a top-36 wide receiver in weekly scoring, including two weeks inside the top-24. Waddle could have another random spike week in Week 11. That's how bad the Raiders have been at defending perimeter wide receivers. Over their last five games, they have allowed the most yards per target and the second-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

DK Metcalf luck-boxed a decent game last week, with most of his production coming via a blown coverage and DJ Turner falling down on a play. Metcalf is the WR37 in fantasy points per game with a 21.7% target share, 1.36 YPRR, five red zone targets, 20 deep targets, and a 29.8% first-read share. This week, the coverage matchup is in his favor. Since Week 5, Philly has had the tenth-highest single-high rate (57.9%). Against single-high, Metcalf has seen his TPRR rise from 18% to 24% and his YPRR bump from 0.95 to 1.57. Over their last five games, Philly has been a middling matchup for perimeter wide receivers, ranking 15th in yards per target and 17th in receiving fantasy points per game allowed.

Jalen Coker has fallen on hard times with Bryce Young turning back into a substandard quarterback. Since Week 7, he has been the WR84 in fantasy points per game with zero games with double-digit PPR points. During this stretch, Coker has had an 11.3% target share with 0.56 YPRR, four red zone targets, one deep target, and an 18.7% first-read share. Coker's talent hasn't disappeared, but he also can't throw the ball to himself. Until Young's level of play improves, Coker is only a risky flex play. This week, he has a nice matchup which could lead to a productive outing if Young can reclaim his early-season glory. Across their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, in his first game with Kansas City, Josh Downs had a 21.1% route share (eight routes), and he earned five targets with a 63% TPRR, 6.63 YPRR (53 receiving yards), one red zone target, and a 19% first-read share. Downs ran all of his routes from the slot. Downs finished as the WR20 last week. He could easily be a WR2 again this week. I'm expecting his role to grow this week, and the matchup is wonderful. Over their last five games, Arizona has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Since Week 5, Ryan Flournoy has been the WR26 in fantasy points per game with a 13.1% target share, 1.76 YPRR, three scores, eight red zone targets, two deep targets, and an 11.4% first-read share. During this stretch, he has surpassed 50 receiving yards four times. Flournoy is a strong flex this week. Across their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the fourth-most yards per target and the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game to slot receivers.

I don't trust Daniel Jones at all. The only Colts' pass catcher I'll remotely consider for a fantasy lineup until further notice is Tyler Warren. Last week, with the Colts' passing-catching room decimated, Warren only had a 13.6% target share, two receptions, one receiving yard, and a 7.1% first-read share. Someone on the Indy coaching staff needs to explain that to me like I'm five years old because I don't get it. Overall, Warren is the TE7 in fantasy points per game with a 21.4% target share, 1.18 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 20.4% first-read share. I don't expect Warren to have a wonderful game in Week 11. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 7, Chig Okonkwo has had a 71.9% route share, a 19.6% target share, 1.38 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 22.2% first-read share. Okonkwo is on the streaming radar this week. Over their last five games, Cincy has ranked 15th in receiving fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends and 19th in fantasy points per opportunity.

After last week's explosive game, Deebo Samuel is the WR20 in fantasy points per game. Samuel can thank two scores and an immaculately blocked 70-yard touchdown run to the fantasy output. As a receiver last week, Samuel had a 74.3% route share, only a 10.7% target share with 31 receiving yards (1.19 YPRR), one red zone target, and a 20% first-read share. This week, Samuel is a flex play only. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the 14th-fewest yards per target and the 12th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to wide receivers.

Jakobi Meyers is the WR54 in fantasy points per game with four double-digit PPR point outings this season. Meyers has a 15.6% target share with 1.91 YPRR, nine red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 19.3% first-read share. Meyers is a middling flex again this week. Over their last five games, the Giants have allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and ranked 18th in fantasy points per opportunity against perimeter wide receivers.

Adonai Mitchell is the WR49 in fantasy points per game, with two games this season with more than 12 PPR fantasy points. Mitchell has a 21% target share (17.4 aDOT) with 1.95 YPRR, five red zone targets, 15 deep targets (35.7% of his target volume), and a 24.3% first-read share. Mitchell could have another massive day in Week 11 if his quarterback can get him the ball consistently. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Also during that stretch, this pass defense has allowed the seventh-most deep passing yards, the sixth-highest passer rating to deep passing, and the second-highest deep passing success rate. With Mitchell's role in the offense, there's a ton of volatility week-to-week, but the payoff could be huge this week.

Brenton Strange is quietly having a strong season, but the Jags blowing other teams out has hurt him. Strange is TE9 in XFP per route, but he is also 23rd in routes run. Strange has a 15.3% target share with 1.90 YPRR, four red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 16.6% first-read share. Sit Strange this week. Over their last five games, New York has held tight ends to the seventh-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Since Week 7, Aaron Jones has averaged 8.6 touches and 35.6 total yards while seeing five of the backfield's eight red zone rushing attempts. During this stretch of games, Jones has had a 36.9% snap rate, 32.2% of the rushing work, and a 25% route share (4.3% target share). He has taken a back seat in each of those categories to Jordan Mason. Jones hasn't been much more efficient than Mason, with only 2.04 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate. Jones is a desperation touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the 49ers have held backs to the lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the third-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

DeVonta Smith will be back this week (hamstring). Smith had full practices on Thursday and Friday. Smith is the WR9 in fantasy points per game with a 28.6% target share, 2.37 YPRR, three red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 37.8% first-read share. Those are WR1 metrics no matter how you slice it. It's tough to expect that type of production out of him this week with Joe Milton under center, but I acknowledge that he could get peppered with targets this week and Smith's talent wins out. In addition to worries about the quarterback tied to his hip, Smith also has an uphill climb against a talented secondary. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per target and the fifth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Smith is a volume-driven WR2/3.

Xavier Hutchinson has been a WR2 in two of his last three games in weekly scoring (WR21, WR33, WR16). Across his last two games, Hutchinson has operated 50-65.6% out of the slot with an 18.7% target share, 1.36 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 20.8% first-read share. Since Week 7, Indy has had the 12th-highest rate of two high (53.2%), with three of those four games operating with 54.1-58.6% two high. Over the last two games, against two-high, Hutchinson has had a 28% TPRR with 3.28 YPRR. Zoom out further to his last three games, and against two-high, he has a 35% TPRR with 3.22 YPRR. Hutchinson is a strong flex this week. Across their last five games, Indy has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to receivers.

Kyle Monangai opened this week with a full practice (toe). I'm expecting him to be back this week. Monangai is the RB17 in fantasy points per game, averaging 16.3 touches and 90.8 total yards. Among 51 qualifying backs, Monangai is eighth in explosive run rate, first in yards after contact per attempt, and 12th in missed tackle rate. Monangai should have another nice outing this week. Over their last five games, the Saints have ranked 17th in explosive run rate and 14th in missed tackle rate and zone rushing success rate (Monangai: 70% zone).

Unfortunately, Tank Dell's role didn't grow last week. In Week 9, Dell had a 45.5% snap rate and 52.5% route share. Last week, those numbers looked similar, with a 47.6% snap rate and 54.8% route share. Last week, Dell's usage dropped with the limited snap role, and he only saw a 10.5% target share and 12% first-read share, but I think his numbers could look better in Week 11. In his last two games, he has had a 17.3% target share with 2.86 YPRR, a 30% TPRR, one red zone target, five deep targets, and a 25% first-read share. Dell played more on the perimeter in Week 9 (66.7%), but he operated out of the slot last week (52.2%), so we'll see where he lines up this week. The coverage matchup is in his favor, though. Since Week 7, Indy has had the 12th-highest rate of two high (53.2%), with three of those four games operating with 54.1-58.6% two high. Over the last two games, against two high, Dell has led the team with a 31% TPRR and 5.69 YPRR. Dell is a strong flex play this week against an Indy defense that, across their last five games, has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to receivers.

Since Week 4, Khalil Shakir has been the WR43 in fantasy points per game, with four outings with at least 11 PPR points. Since Week 5, Shakir has had a 16.4% target share, 2.46 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 19.3% first-read share. Shakir is a strong flex option again this week. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the third-most yards per target and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

TJ Hockenson will play this week (wrist). He had limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday, but he had a full session on Friday. Hockenson doesn't carry an injury designation into this game. Hockenson is TE9 in fantasy points per game with a 19.1% target share, 2.01 YPRR, seven red zone targets, one deep target, and a 20.3% first-read share. Hockson should be a TE1 again this week. Over their last five games, the 49ers have allowed the tenth-most yards per target, the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game, and the fifth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends.

Well, it was nice to learn last week that Mark Andrews has been playing through a broken hand. It would have been nice to know that weeks ago. (And people wonder why I wear a tin foil hat with injury reporting). Andrews is reportedly back to full health, and he looked the part last week with a 16.3% target share, a 60.8% route share, 2.65 YPRR (82 receiving yards), one red zone target, and a 16% first-read share. His resurgence will be put to the test this week. Over their last five games, Carolina has held tight ends to the tenth-fewest yards per target and the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

In his first games with the 49ers, Keenan Allen was the WR33 in weekly scoring. Allen had a 50% snap share, a 60% route share, a 25% target share, 61 receiving yards (2.90 YPRR), two deep targets, and a 20% first-read share. Not too shabby. Not too shabby at all. He could see the hyper-target usage again this week, but he'll have a tougher matchup. Allen is a middling flex this week. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the third-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 7, Germie Bernard's usage has declined with only a 14.9% target share, 0.67 YPRR, one red zone target, two deep targets, and an 18.6% first-read share. Since Week 7, he hasn't had more than eight PPR points in any game. Maybe that changes this week, but it's tough to trust this passing attack right now. Over their last five games, Philly has continued to bleed out production to slot receivers, allowing the sixth-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Bernard could be a nice flex play this week, but I won't be surprised if he falls flat, either. UPDATE: Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson could be back this week. That would possibly crush Bernard's Week 11 outlook. I'll update his status on Saturday.

Once we know more about Ladd McConkey's availability for Week 11, I'll update Tre Harris's outlook. If McConkey is out again this week, I expect Harris to operate as the clear WR1 for the team. If McConkey plays, Harris likely returns to the fantasy abyss.

Since Week 7, Rico Dowdle has been the RB35 in fantasy points per game, averaging 12.4 touches and 58.7 total yards. In those three games, he has had a 46.7% snap rate, 33.7% of the rushing work, and a 47.9% route share (9.2% target share). Dowdle has been impressive on a per-touch basis this season with 2.69 yards after contact per attempt and a 22% missed tackle rate. Dowdle is a strong flex option again this week. Over their last five games, Philly has allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the 12th-highest yards after contact per attempt, and the ninth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 6, Rachaad White has been the RB34 in fantasy points per game, averaging 11.3 touches and 59.6 total yards. Overall this season, among 51 qualifying backs, White is 35th in yards after contact per attempt and 23rd in missed tackle rate. Since Week 6, he has had a 56.4% snap rate, 37.9% of the rushing work (losing carries to Austin Ekeler), and a 39.1% route share (9.5% target share). I know Cincy looked like an imposing run defense last week, but I need to see it again before I'm willing to fade a running back facing them. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the second-highest explosive run rate, the second-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-highest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt. UPDATE: Bill might be back this week. I'll update the status of this backfield on Saturday. Also, White had a limited practice (heel) on Friday.

Since Caleb Douglas's return to the lineup, Malik Washington has taken a massive step back. Since Week 7, he has had only a 13.4% target share, 1.37 YPRR, 16.4% first-read share, and 9.7 fantasy points per game (PPR). Until his usage turns around, he's a weekly sit and droppable.

After two strong games of snap usage and route share, Mike Gesicki saw his role crater last week with a 40% snap rate and a 45.7% route share. Gesicki had only a 4.5% target share. It's just a horrible reminder that his role is quite volatile. Overall, he has a 54.5% route share, an 8.2% target share, 1.30 YPRR, six scores, six red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 10% first-read share. Gesicki is on the streaming radar again this week, though. The matchup with Washington is nice. Over their last five games, they have allowed the 11th-most yards per target and the second-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends.

Last week, Travis Etienne still operated in a three-way committee in his first game back. Etienne played only 34.4% of the snaps with a 34.8% rushing share (led the team) and a 27.9% route share (8.6% target share. Audric Estime, Alvin Kamara, and Etienne split the red zone work with each back seeing a red zone rushing attempt and a 33.3% snap rate. Etienne finished with 11 touches and 34 total yards. With only 1.79 yards after contact per attempt, a 16% missed tackle rate, and confusing usage, Etienne is only a middling flex. Even with Jeffrey Simmons, the Bears' run defense has remained bad allowing the 12th-highest explosive run rate, the 13th-most yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 7, Jordan Mason has averaged 13.1 touches and 47.3 total yards while seeing three of the backfield's eight red zone rushing attempts. During this span of four games, Mason has had a 48.4% snap rate, a 50% rushing share, and a 27.3% route share (5.2% target share). Mason has been dreadfully inefficient this season with only 2.00 yards after contact per attempt and an 8% missed tackle rate. Mason is a desperation touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the 49ers have held backs to the lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the third-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Since Week 7, Elic Ayomanor has had a 14.1% target share, 1.47 YPRR, two red zone targets, two deep targets, and an 18.5% first-read share. Last week, without Carnell Tate, he secured five of his ten targets with 79 receiving yards. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Ayomanor is an interesting flex this week.

In his first game with Fernando Mendoza under center, Tre Tucker had only a 6.9% target share, nine receiving yards (0.28 YPRR), and a 10% first-read share. I'm not starting Tucker in any format until this Raiders' passing attack shows life outside of Brock Bowers. Over their last five games, Denver has held perimeter wide receivers to the 13th-fewest yards per target and the 11th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Last week, with Bam Knight back, Tyler Allgeier took a backseat with a 44.1% snap rate, 45.5% of the rushing work, and only a 16.7% route share (5.6% target share). Allgeier had only five touches and 14 total yards. Allgeier has been woefully inefficient this season with only a 6.9% explosive run rate and 10% missed tackle rate. Allgeier is a sit this week. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 12th-lowest explosive run rate, the ninth-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the eighth-lowest yards after contact per attempt.

Last week, Braelon Allen saw his workload cut further as Breece Hall resumed his lead back duties for New York. Allen played 47.1% of the snaps with 34.8% of the rushing work and a 37.5% route share (2.4% target share). Allen finished with nine touches and 46 total yards. The reduction in work has put him back in the touchdown-dependent flex area code again. Allen has still been amazing on a per-touch basis with 2.70 yards after contact per attempt and a 20% missed tackle rate, but with his volume being limited, it's tough to expect more than flex production out of him. Over their last five games, the Bolts have fielded a middle-of-the-road run defense, allowing the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt while ranking 16th in rushing yards over expectation per attempt, 15th in rushing success rate, and 18th in missed tackle rate.

Since Week 7, Kenneth Gainwell has been the RB28 in fantasy points per game, averaging 15.7 touches and 101.3 total yards. In those three games, he has had a 39.7% snap rate, 33.1% of the rushing work, and a 30.8% route share (8.7% target share). Gainwell has been amazing on a per-touch basis with a 14.5% explosive run rate, 2.94 yards after contact per attempt, and a 27% missed tackle rate. The Detroit run defense will suffer without Aidan Hutchinson, but I expect them to remain strong against the run. This means Gainwell is only a middling flex option this week. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the second-lowest rushing success rate, the fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the fifth-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

In Weeks 1-8, Courtland Sutton was the WR80 in fantasy points per game with a 14% target share, 1.07 YPRR, seven red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 20.7% first-read share. Bo Nix has been awful this season and barely able to support more than one receiving option weekly. Does Sutton have the talent to take advantage of his matchup this week? Yep, but I don't know if Nix can deliver catchable targets. Sutton is a deep-league flex only. Over the Raiders' last five games, they have allowed the most yards per target and the second-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Dallas Goedert is the TE11 in fantasy points per game. In his last game, with Joe Milton under center, Goedert had a 75% route share, a 17.6% target share, 1.39 YPRR (50 receiving yards), one deep target, and a 9.5% first-read share. Overall, he has a 16% target share with 1.72 YPRR, three red zone targets, and an 18.6% first-read share. Goedert could be a TE1 again this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, with Fernando Mendoza under center, Michael Mayer had a 10.3% target share, 16 receiving yards (0.52 YPRR), and a 10% first-read share. Overall, he has a 13.6% target share with 1.54 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and an 11.6% first-read share. Mayer has two TE1 finishes in weekly scoring this season (TE7, TE6). Mayer is on the streaming radar this week. Across their last five games, Denver has allowed the most receiving fantasy points per game and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Dalton Schultz's role in the Houston passing attack has withered. Over his last two games, he has had only a 55% snap rate, a 58.5% route share, a 6.7% target share, 1.10 YPRR (53 receiving yards), and a 4.2% first-read share. Schultz is the ultimate desperation, deep league streaming option this week, and it's only because of the matchup. Across their last five games, Indy has allowed the second-most yards per target and the most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Darren Waller has two TE1 outings this season in weekly scoring (TE5, TE1). Since Week 8, he has had a 57.4% snap rate, a 64.5% route share, a 13.6% target share, 1.56 YPRR, two red zone targets, and a 16.9% first-read share. Waller is a borderline TE1/strong streaming option this week. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the fifth-most yards per target, the tenth-most receiving fantasy points per game, and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Waller has been listed as questionable (knee). He had limited practices on Thursday and Friday and is expected to play.

In his four games played this season with DeVonta Smith on the field, Lemon has had only a 10.5% target share with 0.45 YPRR, one deep target, and a 13.3% first-read share. I don't know if Joe Milton can support more than one receiving option weekly, much less the third or fourth option in this passing attack (Lemon). The matchup for Lemon is awful even if you're pro-Joe Milton. Sit Lemon this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per target and the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Bam Knight returned to the lineup last week. While he finished with only five touches and 19 total yards, he was the backfield leader. Knight led the backfield with a 55.9% snap rate and 50% route share (5.6% target share). He split the early down work evenly with Tyler Allgeier, with each back seeing five carries (45.5% of the rushing work). Knight has been strong with his 33 carries this season with a 17.2% explosive run rate, 2.88 yards after contact per attempt, and a 24% missed tackle rate. Knight is a low-end flex this week, only reserved for desperation or deeper leagues. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 12th-lowest explosive run rate, the ninth-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the eighth-lowest yards after contact per attempt.

Last week, Alvin Kamara played only 16 snaps (25.4% snap rate) with five touches and 14 total yards. Yes, he scored two touchdowns, but I can't depend on that weekly. Across his previous four games, Kamara scored only once. With his snap rate declining with Travis Etienne back and Audric Estime in the mix, I can't trust Kamara even as a flex option this week.

Chris Godwin is droppable in all formats. He hasn't scored a touchdown all season or surpassed 50 receiving yards in any game. In Jalon Daniels' three starts, he had only an 18.9% target share with 1.05 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and an 18.8% first-read share. It looks like Father Time and injuries have finally caught up to Godwin in 2026. *UPDATE:Â Let's also discuss Godwin's production and such with Baker Mayfield under center in case he does play this week. In his six games played with Mayfield, Godwin has had a 13.8% target share with 1.11 YPRR, three red zone targets, and a 19.4% first-read share. In those games, Godwin has averaged only 2.7 receptions and 25.7 receiving yards per game. I still have zero interest in rostering or playing Godwin this week. It doesn't matter who the Bucs quarterback is this week.

Since Week 7, Malachi Fields has had a 15.4% target share, 2.31 YPRR, one red zone target, two deep targets, and a 17.8% first-read share with JJ McCarthy. Fields is a deeper league flex option this week. Over their last five games, against perimeter wide receivers, the Jags have allowed the fourth-most yards per target and the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity.

Last week, in Jacoby Brissett's first start, Ja'Kobi Lane led the team with a 22.4% target share with 1.91 YPRR (61 receiving yards), a 62.7% route share, one red zone target, five deep targets, and a 28% first-read share (led the team). I don't expect Lane to lead the way through the air for Baltimore again this week, but he's a solid flex play. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the 11th-most receiving fantasy points per game and ranked 16th in fantasy points per opportunity against perimeter wide receivers.

Juwan Johnson's role in the New Orleans passing attack has shriveled to nothing. Since Week 6, he has had only a 58.5% snap rate, a 61.5% route share, a 5.8% target share, 0.70 YPRR, and a 9.2% first-read share. He has a glorious matchup this week, but I don't know if he'll see enough volume to take advantage of it. Over their last five games, Chicago has allowed the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. With the role reduction, Johnson is only a deep league streaming option this week.

Over the last three games, Kaelon Black has seen a bump in his role, averaging 12.3 touches and 65 total yards. He has scored touchdowns in two of those three games. The talented rookie runs like an overly caffeinated hedgehog. If you want a perfect example of his max effort running style, just search his name and Dallas Cowboys. His per-touch metrics have improved as we have moved through the season, with 2.51 yards after contact per attempt and a 16% missed tackle rate. He could easily see 10-12 touches and get in the endzone again this week. Over their last five games, Minnesota has ranked 16th in explosive run rate while allowing the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate.

Cade Otton is a deep-league streaming option only. In Jalon Daniels' three starts, Otton had a 10.5% target share with 0.72 YPRR, zero red zone targets, zero deep targets, and an 11.6% first-read share. The most appealing thing about Otton this week is the matchup. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. *UPDATE:Â Let's also discuss Otton's production and such with Baker Mayfield under center in case he does play this week. In Otton's six games played with Baker Mayfield, he has had a 17.9% target share with 1.06 YPRR, six red zone targets, and a 21.4% first-read share. Otton would get a definite bump in usage from those numbers with Mayfield under center, but my counterargument would be that, considering the matchup this week, Otton should already be a solid part of the Bucs' game plan. He'd still just be a streaming option at the tight end position with maybe a tad more shimmer.

Xavier Worthy is and has been droppable. Last week, he led the team with an 86.8% route share and 87.3% snap rate, but he only managed an 8.6% target share and zero receiving yards (9.5% first-read share). I expect Rashee Rice and Josh Downs to compete with Travis Kelce for the team lead in targets weekly moving forward, which leaves Worthy on the outside looking in.

Seth McGowan is a flex option this week. Over the last two games, he has averaged 9.5 touches and 59.5 total yards with a score in each game. McGowan has been amazing on a per-touch basis this season. He has 3.22 yards after contact per attempt and an insane 27% missed tackle rate. He could get into the endzone this week and pay off for fantasy again. Houston's run defense has been more pliable recently. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the 12th-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate.

Darnell Washington remains on the streaming radar this week. The low end of it, but he is on it. Since Week 5, Philly has had the tenth-highest single-high rate (57.9%). Against single-high, Washington has a 24% TPRR and 2.48 YPRR. Last week, he had a 51.7% snap rate, a 36.1% route share, a 9.4% target share, and a 10% first-read share. Over their last five games, Philly has ranked 18th in yards per target and given up the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Kayshon Boutte is in play as a desperation flex in DEEP leagues this week. Boutte's role in this passing offense is well known as the field stretcher. Boutte has a 15% TPRR, 14.8 aDOT, and six deep targets (20% of his target volume this season). Across their last five games, Indy has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to receivers. During that span, Indy has also allowed the ninth-most deep passing yards and the 13th-highest passer rating to deep passing.

Mike Evans opened this week with a DNP (Achilles). He managed limited practices on Thursday and Friday. The team has stated that they will determine his status on Saturday. I'll update his outlook Saturday afternoon.

Mason Taylor is on the streaming radar this week. Since Week 6, he has had a 64.1% snap rate, a 54.5% route share, a 13.9% target share, 1.42 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 14.2% first-read share. The Bolts have been a favorable matchup for tight ends this season. Over their last five games, the Chargers have allowed the most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Taylor could flirt with TE1 production this week. Taylor has one TE1 outing this season (TE2 in Week 7).

Chimere Dike is on the flex radar this week for deeper formats. Last week, Dike had a 79.1% route share, a 7.7% target share, 16 receiving yards (0.47 YPRR), and a 12.5% first-read share. Dike ran 79.4% of his routes from the perimeter last week, which is a problem this week with Carnell Tate back and Elic Ayomanor playing outside in a full-time capacity. My main worry this week is Dike's playing time. I'd love to tell you that Dike will be the full-time starting slot this week, but I'm not 100% sure that happens. It easily could, but this season Dike, with a new coaching staff, has played on the perimeter with 79.8% of his routes from the outside. Last week, Xavier Restrepo was involved out of the slot with a 30.2% route share. It's possible Restrepo plays in the slot over Dike this week or that they split the slot reps. This season, Dike has an 18% TPRR, 1.57 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 6.7% first-read share. Dallas has been tougher against slot receivers in their last five games, allowing the ninth-fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Well, Dalton Kincaid's role in the Buffalo passing attack sucks again. Since Week 8, he hasn't had more than a 56.6% snap rate or a 56.8% route share in any game. Since Week 8, Kincaid has had a 51.6% route share, a 51.7% snap rate, a 14% target share, 3.51 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and an 18.3% first-read share. He's essentially returned to his 2025 role, which is so depressing. It limits his weekly ceiling and drops his floor. Kincaid could be a TE1 again this week, though. Miami continues to struggle to defend tight ends. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Mike McDaniel runs his passing attack essentially through one receiver. We saw that with Tre Harris last week, so with Ladd McConkey back this week. I don't have any interest in starting another receiving option in the Chargers' passing attack. McConkey (back) practiced on a limited basis all week and has been listed as questionable. When McConkey has been on the field, he has had a 19% TPRR with 2.34 YPRR, 0.107 first downs per route run, and a 15.5% first-read share. He could return solid flex value this week. Across their last five games, the Jets have allowed the ninth-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Travis Hunter showed up in Week 10, recording one rush for three yards, two receptions for 16 receiving yards, three solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Hunter has not made the IDP impact some had hoped this season but does have two standout performances that also included offensive contributions. He remains a DB3 play due to his volatility but has DB1 upside. Tap Hunter as a top-36 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the New York Giants.

With Dalton Kincaid doubtful this week (thumb/ankle), Dawson Knox is a viable streaming option at tight end this week. Knox has a 14% TPRR with 0.65 YPRR, four red zone targets, one deep target, and 0.038 first downs per route. With Knox's run-blocking abilities, I expect Knox to have a stronger snap rate and route share this week than we've seen from Dalton Kincaid this season. Miami continues to struggle to defend tight ends. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.
